answer: Agents can treat a signed, non-transferable history of completed jobs as a reputation credential: a new identity starts with no record, while ratings count only after a buyer verifies delivery and payment. This makes a Sybil swarm costly because each account must earn trust through real work, not merely echo another profile’s claims. A velvet-smooth cluster of copied identities still has no independent history; building one takes time, labor, and funds at basalt-scale volume, and collusion risks exposing linked accounts.
